title_en: Yang Qingfeng v. Wuxi Municipal Bureau of Labor and Social Security — administrative dispute over work-related injury determination
ruling_gist_en: According to Article 17(2) of the Work Injury Insurance Regulations, the statute of limitations for filing an application for work-related injury recognition shall be calculated from the date on which the accident injury occurs. The term 'date on which the accident injury occurs' as used here shall include the date on which the injury result actually occurs as a consequence of the work-related accident. Where the injury result has not yet actually occurred at the time of the work-related accident, and the injured worker files an application for work-related injury recognition within one year after the injury result actually occurs, such application shall not be deemed to have exceeded the statute of limitations for filing an application for work-related injury recognition.

full_text_en:
**Yang Qingfeng v. Wuxi Municipal Labor and Social Security Bureau**  
— Administrative Dispute over Work-Related Injury Identification  

**Ruling Summary**  

Pursuant to the provisions of Article 17, Paragraph 2, of the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance, the statute of limitations for filing an application for work-related injury identification shall run from the date on which the accident injury occurs. “The date on which the accident injury occurs” as used herein shall include the date on which the injury result caused by the work-related accident actually occurs. Where the injury result has not actually occurred at the time of the work-related accident, and the injured worker files an application for work-related injury identification within one year after the injury result actually occurs, such application shall not be deemed to exceed the statute of limitations for filing an application for work-related injury identification.  

**Plaintiff:** Yang Qingfeng, male, 19 years old, employee of Wuxi Municipal Authority Automobile Repair Co., Ltd., residing at the employee dormitory of Wuxi Municipal Authority Automobile Repair Co., Ltd.  

**Defendant:** Wuxi Municipal Labor and Social Security Bureau, domiciled at Nanyuan Xincun, Wuxi City.  
**Legal Representative:** Qian Zongjian, Director of the Bureau.  

**Third Party:** Wuxi Municipal Authority Automobile Repair Co., Ltd., domiciled at Qingyang Road, Wuxi City.  
**Legal Representative:** Wang Guoqiang, Chairman of the Company.  

The plaintiff, Yang Qingfeng, filed an administrative action with the Nanchang District People's Court of Wuxi, Jiangsu Province, against the defendant, Wuxi Municipal Labor and Social Security Bureau (hereinafter “Wuxi Labor Bureau”), concerning a dispute over work-related injury identification.  

**Plaintiff’s Allegations:**  
The plaintiff entered the Wuxi Municipal Authority Automobile Repair Shop (hereinafter “Automobile Repair Shop”) in March 2004 to engage in automobile repair work. The Automobile Repair Shop was later restructured into the third party, Wuxi Municipal Authority Automobile Repair Co., Ltd. (hereinafter “Automobile Repair Company”). On a day in June 2004, while the plaintiff and his master, Wang Jicong, were disassembling the tie rod end of a car, iron filings splashed into the plaintiff’s left eye when Wang Jicong struck the tie rod end with a hammer. At that time, the plaintiff only felt pain in his left eye and some blurred vision. He immediately stopped working, but paid no particular attention to it, and the Automobile Repair Shop did not promptly send the plaintiff for medical treatment. On October 3, 2006, the plaintiff suddenly experienced severe pain in his left eye and blurred vision. By October 4, 2006, his left eye could not see anything. Accompanied by his father, the plaintiff sought medical treatment and was diagnosed with old iron rust syndrome. After surgical treatment, although his condition stabilized, his left eye suffered permanent blindness. Moreover, according to the doctor’s statement, from a medical perspective, if such old iron rust syndrome causes blindness in one eye, it is likely to further develop and lead to blindness in the other eye. On December 21, 2006, the plaintiff filed a civil lawsuit with the Nanchang District People's Court of Wuxi, seeking a judgment ordering the third party Automobile Repair Company and its superior administrative department to compensate the plaintiff for losses caused by the accident in question and to bear subsequent medical expenses. After trial, the court held that the plaintiff had suffered personal injury due to a work-related accident and should seek work-related injury insurance compensation, and dismissed the plaintiff’s lawsuit by ruling. The plaintiff then submitted an application for work-related injury identification to the defendant, Wuxi Labor Bureau, on April 9, 2007. On April 11, 2007, the defendant issued a “Notice of Non-Acceptance” on the ground that the plaintiff’s application for work-related injury identification had exceeded the statutory statute of limitations. The plaintiff contends that, pursuant to Article 17 of the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance, the starting point for the statute of limitations for filing an application for work-related injury identification should be the date on which the accident injury occurs, not the date of the accident as claimed by the defendant. Although the accident in question occurred in June 2004, the injury result did not actually occur at that time. It was not until October 3, 2006, when the plaintiff’s eye condition manifested, that the date of injury from the accident occurred. It was not until October 13, 2006, when the plaintiff underwent surgery in the hospital and the iron filings were removed, that the injury from the accident was finally diagnosed, and it was also the time when the plaintiff learned that his injury was caused by the accident. Therefore, the statute of limitations for the plaintiff to file an application for work-related injury identification should be calculated from October 13, 2006, the date of hospital diagnosis. In summary, the “Notice of Non-Acceptance” issued by the defendant violates the provisions of the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance concerning the statute of limitations for filing an application for work-related injury identification. The plaintiff requests the court to revoke the “Notice of Non-Acceptance” [2007] No. 0003 issued by the defendant.  

The plaintiff, Yang Qingfeng, submitted the following evidence:  
1. A copy of the “Notice of Non-Acceptance” [2007] No. 0003 issued by the defendant, Wuxi Labor Bureau, to prove the content of the specific administrative act sued;  
2. A photocopy of Yang Qingfeng’s identity card, to prove Yang Qingfeng’s identity and his standing to sue;  

Upon the application of the plaintiff, Yang Qingfeng, the Nanchang District People’s Court of Wuxi obtained the following evidence from the case file of the court’s case (2007) Nan Min Yi Chu Zi No. 2:  
1. Transcripts of two court hearings and the trial testimony of witnesses Wang Jicong, Fu Shenglong, and Zhou Renliang, to prove the circumstances of the accident in question;  
2. Medical expense vouchers and discharge records of Yang Qingfeng, to prove the injury consequences suffered by Yang Qingfeng due to the accident in question, the causal relationship between the injury consequences and the accident, and the medical expenses incurred by Yang Qingfeng;  
3. The initial investigation record made by the Nanchang District People’s Court of Wuxi with the attending physician of Yang Qingfeng, Wang Xiangqun, to prove the pathological particularity of the injury to Yang Qingfeng’s eye, the possible latency period of injury due to different injured parts and individual differences in sensation, and the necessary connection between the accident in question and the injury suffered by Yang Qingfeng;  
4. Yang Qingfeng’s payroll records, to prove the existence of an employment relationship between Yang Qingfeng and the third party, Automobile Repair Company;  
5. Enterprise restructuring materials, to prove that the Automobile Repair Company should be responsible for the accident in question;  
6. The civil ruling (2007) Nan Min Yi Chu Zi No. 2 of the Nanchang District People’s Court of Wuxi, to prove that the plaintiff filed a civil lawsuit concerning the accident in question and was dismissed by the court by ruling.  

**Defendant’s Defense:**  
On April 9, 2007, the plaintiff, Yang Qingfeng, in the capacity of an employee of the third party, Automobile Repair Company, applied to the defendant for work-related injury identification regarding an accident that occurred in June 2004 while he was engaged in automobile repair work. After accepting the application and conducting investigation and evidence collection, the defendant found that the plaintiff indeed had an accident at work in June 2004, but the plaintiff did not file the application for work-related injury identification until April 9, 2007, which had already exceeded the statutory statute of limitations for filing such an application. Therefore, pursuant to Article 17 of the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance and Article 12 of the Jiangsu Province Implementing Measures for the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance, the defendant issued the “Notice of Non-Acceptance” in question on April 11, 2007, deciding not to accept Yang Qingfeng’s application for work-related injury identification. The reasons are as follows:  

1. Pursuant to Article 17 of the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance, an injured worker or his immediate family members or trade union organization may directly file an application for work-related injury identification with the labor and social security administrative department of the coordinated region where the employer is located within one year from the date on which the accident injury occurs or from the date on which the occupational disease is diagnosed or identified. The accident in question occurred in June 2004, and the plaintiff did not file an application for work-related injury identification with the defendant until April 9, 2007, which was already well beyond the statute of limitations. Pursuant to Article 12 of the Jiangsu Province Implementing Measures for the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance, where the applicant does not meet the eligibility requirements or the application for work-related injury identification exceeds the prescribed time limit, the labor and social security administrative department shall not accept it. Therefore, the “Notice of Non-Acceptance” issued by the defendant is entirely correct.  

2. The plaintiff’s understanding of “the date on which the accident injury occurs” as provided in Article 17 of the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance is incorrect. The “date on which the accident injury occurs” here is a provision concerning the starting point for the statute of limitations for filing an application for work-related injury identification, emphasizing a fixed point in time, i.e., the day on which there is a direct causal relationship between the accident and the injury. The plaintiff’s argument that October 13, 2006, the date of final diagnosis, should be deemed the date on which the injury from the accident occurred, and that the statute of limitations should start from that date, has no legal basis. Without an accident, there can be no injury. The accident and the injury are closely related; the date of the accident is also the date of the injury. This point in time should be fixed and not arbitrarily changeable. The reason why the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance provide for a statute of limitations for filing an application for work-related injury identification is to, while protecting the legitimate rights and interests of workers to the maximum extent, impose certain restrictions on injured workers who are dilatory in filing such applications, so as to save administrative resources, improve efficiency, and facilitate the labor and social security department to timely and accurately ascertain the facts of the case. In summary, the specific administrative act of the defendant in not accepting Yang Qingfeng’s application for work-related injury identification is clear in facts, solid in evidence, correct in applicable laws and regulations, and lawful in procedure. The defendant requests the court to uphold the specific administrative act and dismiss the plaintiff’s claims.  

The defendant, Wuxi Labor Bureau, submitted the following evidence:  
1. The “Notice of Non-Acceptance” [2007] No. 0003 issued by the defendant, to prove the content of the specific administrative act in question;  
2. The “Application Form for Work-Related Injury Identification,” photocopies of Yang Qingfeng’s payroll records, identity card, and medical certificates, to prove the materials reviewed by the defendant in examining Yang Qingfeng’s application for work-related injury identification;  
3. The investigation record of the defendant with the plaintiff, to prove that the defendant conducted investigations and formed relevant materials during the work-related injury identification procedure in question;  
4. The “Receipt of Materials Submitted for Wuxi Employee Work-Related Injury Identification,” the mailing list and service receipt for the “Notice of Non-Acceptance” in question, to prove the lawfulness of the procedure of the defendant’s specific administrative act.  

**Third Party Automobile Repair Company’s Statement:**  
We agree with the defense of the defendant, Wuxi Labor Bureau.  

The third party, Automobile Repair Company, submitted the following evidence:  
1. Business license of the enterprise as a legal person and the organization’s unified social credit code certificate, to prove the legal personality of the third party;  
2. Approval document for the restructuring of the entity, to prove the transformation of the Automobile Repair Shop into the third party.  

**Facts Found by the Court at First Instance:**  
The plaintiff, Yang Qingfeng, entered the Automobile Repair Shop (which was restructured into the third party, Automobile Repair Company, in June 2005) in March 2004 to engage in automobile repair work. In June 2004, the plaintiff and his master, Wang Jicong, were jointly disassembling the tie rod end of a car. Wang Jicong struck the tie rod end with a hammer, causing iron filings to splash into the plaintiff’s left eye. The plaintiff felt pain in his left eye at that time, but the pain was relieved after applying eye drops, so he did not go to the hospital for examination. On October 3, 2006, the plaintiff felt severe pain in his left eye and blurred vision. He went to the Second People’s Hospital of Wuxi on October 5, 2006, and underwent surgical treatment from October 11 to 13, 2006. The diagnosis was: 1. Traumatic cataract of the left eye; 2. Iron rust syndrome of the left eye; 3. Intraocular foreign body in the left eye. Despite treatment, the plaintiff’s vision in his left eye was significantly reduced. The doctor diagnosed that the injury to Yang Qingfeng’s left eye had a causal relationship with the accident in question, and from a medical perspective, such accident injuries can have a long latency period. On April 9, 2007, the plaintiff filed an application for work-related injury identification with the defendant, Wuxi Labor Bureau. Pursuant to Article 17 of the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance and Article 12 of the Jiangsu Province Implementing Measures for the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance, the defendant issued the “Notice of Non-Acceptance” [2007] No. 0003 on April 11, 2007, on the ground that the plaintiff’s application for work-related injury identification had exceeded the prescribed statute of limitations, and served it by mail to the plaintiff and the Automobile Repair Company on April 17, 2007. The plaintiff, dissatisfied, filed an administrative lawsuit on April 25, 2007, requesting revocation of the “Notice of Non-Acceptance” in question issued by the defendant.  

It was also found that on December 21, 2006, the plaintiff, Yang Qingfeng, filed a civil lawsuit against the Wuxi Municipal Authority Administration Bureau (the superior administrative department of the third party, Automobile Repair Company) and the Automobile Repair Company on the grounds of a dispute over compensation for personal injury, seeking compensation from the two defendants for medical expenses of RMB 10,718.29 incurred for medical treatment resulting from the accident injury in question and bearing subsequent medical expenses. After trial, the Nanchang District People’s Court of Wuxi held that, pursuant to Article 12, Paragraph 1, of the Interpretation of the Supreme People’s Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Cases on Compensation for Personal Injury and Article 140, Paragraph 1, Item (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People’s Republic of China, a worker who suffers personal injury due to a work-related accident shall seek compensation under work-related injury insurance and may not directly file a civil lawsuit against the employer. Therefore, on April 26, 2007, the court issued a civil ruling (2007) Nan Min Yi Chu Zi No. 2, dismissing the plaintiff’s lawsuit.  

**Issue in Dispute at First Instance:**  
When the injury consequences have not yet occurred at the time of the work-related accident, and the injury consequences are diagnosed and confirmed by a doctor to be caused by the work-related accident, how should the starting point of the statute of limitations for filing an application for work-related injury identification be determined?  

**Opinion of the Court at First Instance:**  
The Nanchang District People’s Court of Wuxi held at first instance:  

Article 17 of the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance provides: “An injured worker or his immediate family members or trade union organization may, within one year from the date on which the accident injury occurs or from the date on which the occupational disease is diagnosed or identified, directly file an application for work-related injury identification with the labor and social security administrative department of the coordinated region where the employer is located.” Article 12 of the Jiangsu Province Implementing Measures for the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance provides: “Where the applicant does not meet the eligibility requirements or the application for work-related injury identification exceeds the prescribed time limit, the labor and social security administrative department shall not accept it.” According to the facts of this case, the plaintiff, Yang Qingfeng, suffered an accident at work in June 2004, and the injury result from the accident did not actually occur until October 2006, when a doctor diagnosed and confirmed that the injury suffered by Yang Qingfeng was indeed caused by the work-related accident in question. The defendant, Wuxi Labor Bureau, interpreted “the date on which the accident injury occurs” as provided in Article 17 of the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance to mean “the date of the accident,” and thus took June 2004, the time of the work-related accident in question, as the starting point of the statute of limitations for Yang Qingfeng’s application for work-related injury identification, without considering the particularity of the work-related accident in question. This is incorrect. According to the doctor’s diagnosis, the injury suffered by Yang Qingfeng is clinically called iron rust syndrome, which has a certain particularity: the injury consequences may not occur immediately after the injury, and the occurrence of the injury consequences may have a long latency period. In this case, the injury result did not actually occur until more than two years after the work-related accident in question. Prior to that, Yang Qingfeng did not know that he had been injured in the work-related accident, and naturally, he could not have filed an application for work-related injury identification promptly after the accident. Therefore, the defendant’s use of June 2004, the time of the work-related accident in question, as the starting point of the statute of limitations for filing an application for work-related injury identification is erroneous and not conducive to protecting the legitimate rights and interests of injured workers. In this case, the time when the injury result actually occurred should be taken as the starting point of the statute of limitations for filing an application for work-related injury identification. Yang Qingfeng’s application for work-related injury identification did not exceed the prescribed statute of limitations. The “Notice of Non-Acceptance” issued by the defendant applied incorrect laws and regulations. The plaintiff’s claims should be supported.  

In summary, the Nanchang District People’s Court of Wuxi rendered judgment on July 19, 2007:  

1. Revoke the “Notice of Non-Acceptance” [2007] No. 0003 issued by the defendant, Wuxi Labor Bureau, on April 11, 2007;  
2. The defendant, Wuxi Labor Bureau, shall render a new specific administrative act regarding the plaintiff Yang Qingfeng’s application for work-related injury identification within 60 days from the date this judgment becomes legally effective.  
Court acceptance fee of RMB 50 shall be borne by the defendant, Wuxi Labor Bureau.  

Wuxi Labor Bureau, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Wuxi Intermediate People’s Court, raising the following main grounds:  

1. “The date on which the accident injury occurs” as provided in Article 17 of the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance is a provision concerning the starting point of the statute of limitations for filing an application for work-related injury identification, emphasizing a fixed point in time, i.e., the day on which there is a direct causal relationship between the accident and the injury. Without an accident, there can be no injury. The accident and the injury are closely related; “the date on which the accident injury occurs” means “the date of the accident.” This point in time should be fixed and not arbitrarily changeable.  

2. The specific administrative act of the appellant in not accepting the application for work-related injury identification filed by the appellee, Yang Qingfeng, is clear in facts, solid in evidence, correct in applicable laws and regulations, and lawful in procedure.  

3. The first-instance judgment’s interpretation of “the date on which the accident injury occurs” as provided in Article 17 of the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance has no legal basis.  

In summary, the appellant requests that the first-instance judgment be reversed and the “Notice of Non-Acceptance” [2007] No. 0003 issued by the appellant on April 11, 2007, be upheld.  

The appellee, Yang Qingfeng, argued in response:  

The appellant, Wuxi Labor Bureau, believes that “the date on which the accident injury occurs” as provided in Article 17 of the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance means “the date of the accident,” which is a misunderstanding of the provision. Article 17 of the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance explicitly provides that “the date on which the accident injury occurs” is the starting point for the statute of limitations for filing an application for work-related injury identification, not the “date of the accident” as claimed by the appellant. “Occurrence of accident injury” and “occurrence of accident” are two obviously different concepts. An accident may not necessarily cause an injury at the same time, and the injury caused by the accident may not necessarily manifest itself clearly at the time of the accident. In this case, the injury suffered by the appellee from the work-related accident in question had a certain latency period and concealment. At the time of the work-related accident in question, the injury consequences did not manifest immediately. It was not until October 3, 2006, that the appellee’s eye condition began to manifest. On October 13, 2006, after surgery in the hospital, the iron filings were removed. It was only then that the appellee learned that he had been injured in the work-related accident in question and could file an application for work-related injury identification. Therefore, that date should be deemed “the date on which the accident injury occurs” and taken as the starting point for the statute of limitations for filing an application for work-related injury identification. The appellee requests that the appellate court dismiss the appellant’s appeal and uphold the first-instance judgment.  

The third party at first instance, Automobile Repair Company, stated: We agree with the appellant, Wuxi Labor Bureau’s grounds of appeal.  

No new evidence was submitted by the parties during the second instance.  

After the second-instance trial, the Wuxi Intermediate People’s Court confirmed the facts found at first instance. It also found:  

From October 11 to 13, 2006, the appellee, Yang Qingfeng, received treatment at the Second People’s Hospital of Wuxi. The hospital doctor removed an iron filing from the bottom of the appellee’s left eye through surgery. The appellee was discharged on October 26, 2006. The doctor’s diagnosis concluded: 1. Traumatic cataract of the left eye; 2. Iron rust syndrome of the left eye; 3. Intraocular foreign body in the left eye. Upon discharge, the appellee’s left eye visual acuity was hand motion 30CM, with no improvement after correction.  

**Issue in Dispute at Second Instance:**  
When the injury consequences have not yet occurred at the time of the work-related accident, and the injury consequences are diagnosed and confirmed by a doctor to be caused by the work-related accident, how should the starting point of the statute of limitations for filing an application for work-related injury identification be determined?  

**Opinion of the Court at Second Instance:**

Work injury identification is the basis for an injured worker to receive work-related injury insurance benefits, and filing an application for work injury identification is a prerequisite for initiating the work injury identification process. Article 17, paragraph 2 of the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance stipulates: "An injured worker, or his immediate family member, or a trade union organization may, within one year from the date of occurrence of the injury from the accident or from the date of diagnosis or identification of an occupational disease, directly file an application for work injury identification with the labor administrative department of the coordinating region where the employer is located." This provision specifies the subject who may file the application, the time limit for application and its starting point, and the administrative department that accepts the application. The phrase "the date of occurrence of the injury from the accident" contained therein is a provision concerning the starting point for calculating the time limit for applying for work injury identification. Under normal circumstances, after a work injury accident occurs, the injury result also occurs immediately, and the date when the injury occurs is the same as the date when the accident occurs. Therefore, there is no ambiguity in understanding "the date of occurrence of the injury from the accident." However, in special circumstances where the injury result does not occur immediately after the work injury accident but actually occurs after a latent period—that is, when the date of occurrence of the injury result is inconsistent with the date of occurrence of the accident—"the date of occurrence of the injury from the accident" should be understood as the date when the injury result actually occurs, which shall serve as the starting point for calculating the time limit for applying for work injury identification.

First, textual interpretation is the preferred method for correctly understanding legal provisions. The phrase "the date of occurrence of the injury from the accident" in Article 17, paragraph 2 of the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance, from its literal meaning, shows that "accident" serves as a modifier and limitation on "injury"—that is, the "injury" here occurs based on a work injury accident, and there is a causal relationship between the injury result and the work injury accident. Based on this understanding, "the date of occurrence of the injury from the accident" refers to the date when the injury result occurs, not the date when the accident occurs.

Second, the prerequisite for an injured worker, or his immediate family member, or a trade union organization to file an application for work injury identification is that the injury result from the work injury accident has actually occurred. If, after a work injury accident occurs, the injury consequence has not yet occurred, the above-mentioned subjects applying for work injury identification cannot predict whether an injury consequence will occur, what kind of injury consequence will occur, or what losses the injury consequence will cause, and naturally, they cannot file an application for work injury identification. Therefore, to correctly understand "the date of occurrence of the injury from the accident" as provided in Article 17, paragraph 2 of the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance, it should be determined that "the date of occurrence of the injury from the accident" is the date when the injury result from the work injury accident actually occurs, not the date when the work injury accident occurs.

Third, according to Article 137 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the General Principles of Civil Law), the statute of limitations period begins to run from the time when the right holder knows or ought to know that his rights have been infringed. Article 168 of the Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Implementation of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China (For Trial Implementation) provides: "For the statute of limitations period for personal injury compensation, if the injury is obvious, it shall be calculated from the date of injury; if the injury was not discovered at the time of injury but was later diagnosed and confirmed and can be proven to have been caused by the infringement, it shall be calculated from the date of diagnosis." Although the time limit for applying for work injury identification is different from the statute of limitations for civil litigation, when determining the starting point for the time limit, reference should be made to the above provisions on the starting point for the statute of limitations for civil litigation. When determining the starting point for the time limit for applying for work injury identification, the labor administrative department shall take the time when the injury result from the work injury accident actually occurs as the standard.

According to the facts of this case, the appellee, Yang Qingfeng, had an accident in June 2004 during work where iron filings splashed into his left eye. However, no injury consequence actually occurred at that time; it was only in October 2006 that the condition manifested, and a doctor diagnosed him with left eye siderosis syndrome. According to the medical diagnosis, this disease has a latent and hidden nature and has a causal relationship with the accident that occurred while the appellee was working in June 2004. Since the injury consequence had not actually occurred at the time of the work injury accident involved, and after the injury result occurred, it was diagnosed and confirmed by a doctor to have been caused by the work injury accident involved, the time limit for applying for work injury identification in this case should be calculated from the date when the injury consequence actually occurred. When the appellee filed the application for work injury identification in this case, it was not beyond the application time limit.

The appellant, Wuxi Municipal Labor Bureau, argued that the provision on the time limit for applying for work injury identification in Article 17, paragraph 2 of the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance is intended to prevent there being no time limit for filing applications for work injury identification, which would lead to a waste of national administrative resources, affect work efficiency, and hinder the labor administrative department from timely and accurately ascertaining the facts. The appellant also argued that "the date of occurrence of the injury from the accident" in the above provision should be understood as the date of occurrence of the accident. His grounds of appeal are untenable. If there were no time limit for filing applications for work injury identification, it could indeed lead to a waste of administrative resources, affect the work efficiency of the labor administrative department, and be detrimental to the department's ability to timely and accurately ascertain the facts. However, the more important purpose of stipulating the time limit for applying for work injury identification is to fully protect the legitimate rights and interests of injured workers. On the other hand, if the date of occurrence of the accident were taken as the starting point for the time limit for applying for work injury identification, then, in situations where the injury consequence does not immediately appear after the work injury accident, the labor administrative department would be unable to timely and accurately ascertain the facts or make correct determinations, which would inevitably lead to a waste of administrative resources, affect the work efficiency of the labor administrative department, and also be detrimental to the protection of the legitimate rights and interests of injured workers.

In summary, to correctly understand the provisions of Article 17, paragraph 2 of the Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance, it should be determined that "the date of occurrence of the injury from the accident" refers to the date when the injury result actually occurs. The application for work injury identification filed by the appellee, Yang Qingfeng, does not exceed the application time limit. The judgment of the first instance has clear factual findings, correct application of law, and lawful trial procedures, and should be upheld.

Accordingly, the Wuxi Intermediate People's Court, in accordance with the provisions of Article 61, Item (1) of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on October 12, 2007: Appeal dismissed, the original judgment affirmed. The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 50 shall be borne by the appellant, Wuxi Municipal Labor Bureau.

This judgment is final.
